current.text: Garland is the Clippers' starting point guard and main ball handler.
Kawhi Leonard and James Harden are gone and Brandon Ingram is out injured, so Garland is the Clippers' highest-usage player and their best player.
The Clippers roster is not set up to hand the offense to rookies. A rookie guard will not take over his role.
After the trade to the Clippers he played about 30 minutes a night with about 20 points and 7 assists on 29% usage. He ranked 37th per game after the deadline.
Experts expect at least that production this season, with about 30% usage and about 32 minutes if healthy.
A toe injury limited him last season. He is expected to be ready for opening night.
Experts see him as a likely top 30 player, and a healthy Garland might be top 20.
Experts say his market price is too low. They are happy to take him in the 40s or in round 3. Taking him in the 30s is risky.
In an auction mock he went for 25 USD, which Josh called a little under value. Josh's max of 30 USD is probably aggressive.
He is the best fantasy target on the Clippers.
The Clippers might rest him or ease off late in the season because they have no strong reason to win or lose. Experts call this risk small and say his value outweighs it.
The Clippers play 4-3-4 games in our fantasy playoff weeks and have one of the lowest back-to-back totals in the league with 13.

durable.text: Assists are his best category and a real outlier against the league.
He commits many turnovers, a clear weakness against the league and against guards.
He is a poor rebounder even in 30 minutes, and this is a lasting weakness.
He is an electric offensive player and a below-average defender.
He has persistent knee and toe problems and has also had a broken face.
His production drops for a long time after any injury, so he is hard to trust unless fully fit.

note: Garland is the Clippers' top usage option. Experts call him a likely top 30 player, but the market has him around 53 to 65. Yahoo values him at 18 USD and ESPN at 10 USD, and he went for 11 USD in our league last season, so 20 to 25 USD looks fair and his upside is higher. He fits a punt TO build well: assists are his real outlier, he adds threes, points and FT%, and he hurts mainly turnovers and rebounds. Early in the season, check that his toe holds up and that he plays about 32 minutes.
